description: A four-part rhythm sequencer: sixteen steps of kick, snare, hihat and percussion per bar, drawn from eight genres of twelve patterns each

params.text: Chooses one of twelve patterns within the genre; the display names the one selected
At kit the snare part follows GENRE and PATTERN; the seven positions above it lock the snare to another genre's bank
At kit the hihat part follows GENRE and PATTERN; the seven positions above it lock the hihat to another genre's bank
At kit the percussion part follows GENRE and PATTERN; the seven positions above it lock the percussion to another genre's bank
Chooses one of eight pattern banks: Techno, House, Pulse, Broken, Machine, Collapse, Ghost and Drive
Takes the kick out while it is down, leaving the other three parts playing
Switches to the pattern six places along, and back again on a second press; either change takes effect at the start of the next bar

inputs.text: One pulse per quarter note. Each pulse is divided into four sixteenth-note steps
A rising edge above 2V puts the sequence back to the first step of the bar, taking effect on the next clock pulse
0-10V crossfades the snare, hihat and percussion towards the next pattern, deciding each step at random; the kick is left alone
Above 2V it takes the kick out, as holding DROP down does
A rising edge above 2V flips the VARIATION setting over, moving the panel button with it

outputs.text: A 10V gate 3ms long on every kick step
A 10V gate 3ms long on every snare step
A 10V gate 3ms long on every hihat step
A 10V gate 3ms long on every percussion step

notes: nothing plays until a clock arrives at CLOCK; all four outputs stay at 0V until the first pulse
a part locked away from kit keeps the pattern number it held the last time it was at kit, so it stops following PATTERN and MORPH until it is set back
menu: 1 PPQN (Submit standard) — reads each pulse at CLOCK as one quarter note and generates the other three sixteenths
4 PPQN (compatibility) — reads each pulse at CLOCK as one sixteenth note, the timing older patches were built on
